heading: Mortgage & Housing Calculators
title: Mortgage & Housing Calculators - Payments, PMI & Refinancing
description: Choose mortgage, PMI, FHA, VA, refinance, payoff and rent-versus-buy calculators. Compare housing costs with clear U.S. loan assumptions.
intro: Start with the housing decision you need to make: buying, reducing interest, refinancing or renting. These tools estimate costs from your inputs; lender approval, insurance pricing and local ownership costs require separate verification.
guides: Estimate a purchase payment
Use Mortgage for fixed-rate principal and interest plus entered ownership costs. House Affordability and Down Payment help explore a budget before comparing loan offers.
Check insurance and loan programs
Use PMI for conventional borrower-paid insurance. FHA uses a separate MIP model, while VA has its own funding-fee assumptions. These tools do not determine program eligibility.
Compare ways to reduce costs

Mortgage Payoff and Biweekly explore repayment changes; Discount Points compares actual rate and fee quotes. Refinance compares a replacement loan, including entered closing costs. Recast compares a lower payment after a lump sum against keeping the current payment; the existing rate and remaining term are retained.
differences: Mortgage vs. House Affordability
Mortgage estimates a payment for entered loan terms. House Affordability works from an income and debt budget; its result is not preapproval.
PMI vs. FHA MIP
Conventional PMI cancellation and FHA MIP duration follow different conditions. Select the tool that matches the actual loan program.
Biweekly vs. Mortgage Payoff
Biweekly assumes 26 credited periods per year and includes an equal-budget monthly comparison. Mortgage Payoff offers other extra-principal schedules.
Recast vs. Payoff vs. Refinance
Recast spreads a reduced balance across the same remaining contractual term. Payoff explores paying faster while keeping a payment. Refinance replaces the loan and may change rate and term.
questions: Does a mortgage payment include every homeownership expense?
Only the costs included in the selected tool and inputs are modeled. Check property taxes, home insurance, PMI or MIP, HOA, maintenance and transaction costs separately.
Can I compare a conventional loan with FHA or VA?
Yes, using the separate tools with the same price and consistent assumptions. Review differences in insurance, funding fees and eligibility with the lender.
Will a lower payment always save money?
No. A longer term, upfront points or financed closing costs may reduce the monthly payment while increasing total cost. Compare interest, fees, remaining principal and your expected holding period.

heading: Loan & Debt Calculators
title: Loan & Debt Calculators - Payments, APR & Debt Payoff
description: Compare loan payments, vehicle financing, credit cards and debt payoff strategies. Understand APR, repayment timing and borrowing costs.
intro: Choose a calculator for the balance you are financing or repaying. Start with the contract terms, compare both payment size and total cost, then check whether the modeled payment fits your budget. U.S. lender and servicing terms can differ from these estimates.
guides: Estimate a loan or payment
Loan and Payment cover standard borrowing scenarios. Personal Loan and Student Loan include their own supported fee or repayment assumptions; check each page before comparing.
Compare vehicle financing
Auto Loan, Auto Lease and Cash Back or Low Interest answer different purchase decisions. Boat Loan and Lease provide additional financing comparisons.
Plan debt repayment
Use Credit Card Payoff for one balance, Multiple Credit Card Payoff for multiple cards, and Debt Payoff for strategy comparisons. Debt Consolidation compares a replacement borrowing plan.
Choose a repayment order

Debt Snowball prioritizes smaller balances; Debt Avalanche prioritizes higher APRs. Both show account-by-account milestones and a paired comparison. The existing combined Debt Payoff tool retains both modes. Minimums must still be covered.
differences: Loan vs. APR
Loan focuses on payments and interest. APR accounts for the fees and cash-flow timing supported by its model; review official lender disclosures before choosing an offer.
Debt Payoff vs. Debt Consolidation
Debt Payoff reallocates payments among existing debts. Debt Consolidation models replacing debts with new financing, which may introduce fees or a longer term.
Monthly payment vs. total borrowing cost
A smaller payment can come from a longer repayment term. Compare fees, interest, payoff time and any collateral or guarantee obligations alongside the payment.
questions: Does the calculator tell me whether a lender will approve my application?
No. Approval depends on lender underwriting, credit, income, collateral and program requirements beyond the entered calculation.
Can I use the same rate for APR and interest rate?
They may differ. Interest rate determines modeled interest accrual, while disclosed APR can include certain borrowing fees. Use the input definition shown by each tool.
Which debt payoff strategy should I choose?
Compare the modeled interest and payoff dates under a payment budget you can maintain. Promotional terms, minimum-payment rules and fees may change actual results.

heading: Savings & Investment Calculators
title: Savings & Investment Calculators - Growth, Interest & Returns
description: Explore savings goals, compound growth, CDs, investment returns and fees. Compare financial assumptions, inflation and cash-flow timing.
intro: Choose between a savings goal, a growth projection and an investment-return comparison. Keep deposit timing, taxes, fees and inflation consistent when comparing scenarios. Assumed investment returns are hypothetical and do not guarantee a future balance.
guides: Plan savings and cash reserves

Savings solves supported balance and contribution goals. CD estimates a time-deposit outcome, while Emergency Fund, Budget and College Cost help organize personal planning assumptions. Treasury Bill calculates maturity profit from a discount rate or price; Tax Equivalent Yield compares annual yields under entered tax assumptions.
Project growth or compare investments
Investment and Compound Interest model contributions and growth. ROI, CAGR, IRR and Average Return measure different aspects of performance; fees and taxes may change the comparison.
Check rates, timing and purchasing power

Interest and Simple Interest use different accrual conventions. Finance, Present Value and Future Value handle cash-flow timing, while Inflation and Real Return help distinguish nominal from purchasing-power results.
differences: Savings vs. Compound Interest
Savings supports goal-oriented calculations. Compound Interest supports growth and rate-conversion modes; choose the mode that matches deposits and compounding.
ROI vs. CAGR vs. IRR
ROI is a gain relative to cost, CAGR smooths endpoint growth, and IRR reflects modeled cash-flow timing. They are not interchangeable performance measures.
CD yield vs. investment return
A deposit product has contractual terms that must be checked with its issuer. An investment projection uses uncertain return assumptions and can involve loss of principal.
CD vs. Treasury Bill vs. Tax Equivalent Yield

CD projects compounded deposit earnings; Treasury Bill compares purchase cost with face value at maturity. Tax Equivalent Yield converts annual yields under tax assumptions, without equating credit risk or forecasting prices.
questions: Are the default return and inflation rates forecasts?
No. They are editable planning assumptions. Test multiple scenarios and review the methodology and scope of the selected tool.
Should I compare nominal or inflation-adjusted balances?
Use nominal values for future dollar amounts and inflation-adjusted values for purchasing-power comparisons. Keep all inputs and cash flows on a consistent basis.
Are taxes, fees and early withdrawals always included?
No. Coverage differs by tool and selected mode. Include supported inputs and verify account terms, tax treatment and withdrawal restrictions separately.

heading: Retirement Planning Calculators
title: Retirement Planning Calculators - Savings, Accounts & Income
description: Choose retirement, 401(k), IRA, pension, annuity and RMD calculators. Explore savings goals, account growth and retirement income with explicit assumptions.
intro: Choose a tool for the retirement decision in front of you: how much to save, how an account may grow, or how to draw income later. Start with Retirement for an overall savings and withdrawal estimate, then use the account-specific tools to examine the assumptions behind it.
guides: Build a retirement savings target

Use the Retirement Calculator to connect your current savings, time to retirement and planned withdrawals. Try more than one return and inflation assumption rather than treating one projection as a forecast.
Explore retirement accounts

Use 401(k) to examine contributions and an entered employer match. Traditional IRA and Roth IRA address different tax treatments. Check the selected tool’s supported years, limits and eligibility assumptions before comparing results.
Plan income and withdrawals

Use Annuity Payout for payment size or duration, RMD for a required-distribution estimate, and Pension for the modeled benefit options. Social Security provides an estimate under its stated assumptions; confirm your personal benefit record with the Social Security Administration.
Check a Coast FIRE milestone

Coast FIRE estimates how much invested now could grow to an entered retirement target without future deposits. It also models continued investments until that milestone. It does not fund living costs before retirement or guarantee a safe withdrawal rate.
Choose a FIRE spending plan

Use FIRE for a direct annual budget, Lean FIRE to itemize essential spending, or Fat FIRE to separate baseline costs from lifestyle extras. All three size a full target under entered assumptions; Coast FIRE answers the separate question of stopping contributions before a later retirement date.
differences: Retirement vs. 401(k)

Retirement models an overall savings and withdrawal plan. A 401(k) calculation focuses on that account’s contributions, employer match and growth; it does not represent every source of retirement income.
Traditional IRA vs. Roth IRA

Traditional and Roth accounts differ in when taxes may apply. Compare consistent contributions and tax assumptions, and distinguish an account-growth illustration from a determination of contribution eligibility or deductibility.
Annuity accumulation vs. Annuity Payout
Annuity projects an accumulating balance. Annuity Payout explores drawing from a balance. Neither calculation is an insurer quote or a guarantee of lifetime payments.
RMD vs. a withdrawal plan
An RMD estimates a required distribution under the selected rules. It does not establish a sustainable spending amount or cover every exception and inherited-account situation.
Lean FIRE vs. Fat FIRE vs. Coast FIRE

Lean and Fat FIRE organize different spending plans using the same full-target math; neither has a universal dollar cutoff. Coast FIRE discounts a future target to a threshold today. A target crossing does not establish safe withdrawals or fund pre-retirement living costs.
questions: Are the projected returns guaranteed?
No. Entered returns simplify uncertain future outcomes. Fixed-return projections do not capture the full effect of market volatility or the order of investment returns.
Should I include inflation?
Keep income targets, returns and expenses on a consistent basis. A future dollar amount buys less when prices rise; review how the chosen tool treats inflation before comparing scenarios.
Can I add all of these results together?
Only after checking for overlapping balances and income sources. A retirement total that already includes an IRA should not have that same IRA balance added a second time.

heading: Tax & Income Calculators
title: Tax & Income Calculators - Federal Tax, Paychecks & Salary
description: Find U.S. federal income tax, take-home pay, salary, commission, marriage tax, estate tax and sales tax calculators. Choose the tool for your income question.
intro: Start with the amount you want to understand: annual federal income tax, take-home pay, gross salary or a separate transaction tax. These tools cover different calculations; a paycheck estimate and a tax-return estimate are not interchangeable.
guides: Estimate annual federal income tax

Use the Federal Income Tax Calculator for the supported tax year, filing status and entered income, deductions and credits. Review the included taxes and limitations; this is an estimate rather than a filed return.
Understand pay and earnings

Use Paycheck Calculator to estimate net pay under the available payroll assumptions. Salary converts gross earnings between pay periods and work schedules. Commission calculates earnings from an entered rate and sales amount.
Check a specific tax question

Marriage Tax compares the modeled filing scenarios. Estate Tax addresses its stated federal estate-tax assumptions, while Sales Tax calculates a purchase tax from the rate you supply. These tools do not automatically determine all state and local obligations.
differences: Income tax vs. paycheck withholding
Income tax estimates an annual liability. Withholding is money paid toward tax through payroll. A refund or balance due also depends on payments, withholding and credits, not just the gross salary.
Salary conversion vs. take-home pay
Salary converts earnings using hours, workdays and pay periods. It does not turn gross pay into net pay. Use the paycheck tool for the tax and deduction assumptions it supports.
Marginal vs. effective tax rate
A marginal rate applies to the next taxable dollar within a bracket. An effective rate summarizes tax relative to the income measure used; the two percentages answer different questions.
questions: Which tax year should I choose?
Choose the year the income belongs to and verify that the calculator supports it. Filing a return in a later calendar year does not change the tax year of the income.
Does the federal tax estimate include every tax I owe?
No. Check the calculator’s scope for payroll taxes and other adjustments. State, local, self-employment and special tax situations may require separate calculations or professional guidance.
Can these tools tell me my exact refund?
Only modeled inputs are considered. An actual refund depends on the completed return and payments already made. Verify withholding records, credits and other income before relying on an estimate.

heading: Business Calculators
title: Business Calculators - ROAS, Landed Cost & Financial Ratios
description: Explore business calculators for advertising ROAS, landed cost, quick and current ratios, loan payments, profit margin, markup and break-even sales.
intro: Choose a business calculator for advertising returns, shipment acquisition costs, short-term liquidity, pricing or financing. Match the tool to the question: revenue returned by advertising is different from profit, and a balance-sheet liquidity ratio is different from a cash-flow forecast.
guides: Estimate financing payments
Business Loan models payments and borrowing costs from entered loan terms and supported fees. Use actual lender quotes when comparing offers; an estimated payment is not a financing approval.
Set prices and sales targets
Margin and Markup work from different percentage bases. Use Break-Even to connect fixed costs with selling price and variable cost per unit, then explore what happens if costs or prices change.
Explore asset depreciation

Depreciation spreads an entered depreciable amount using the selected method. Review the supported methods and assumptions; a planning schedule does not automatically establish the tax deduction allowed for a particular asset.
Review advertising and shipment costs

ROAS compares attributed revenue with advertising spend or explores contribution-based break-even and target scenarios. Landed Cost adds manually entered acquisition charges for a shipment; it does not fetch tariff rates or classify goods.
Check business liquidity

Current Ratio includes entered current assets; Quick Ratio excludes inventory, prepayments and other non-quick assets. Use balances from the same date and review the quality and timing of those balances.
differences: Margin vs. markup
Margin expresses profit as a share of selling price; markup expresses profit as a share of cost. At a cost of $80 and a price of $100, profit is $20, margin is 20% and markup is 25%.
Break-even sales vs. profit
Break-even covers the entered fixed and variable costs without a remaining operating profit in the model. A profit target requires additional sales or a change in costs or pricing.
Depreciation vs. loan payments
Depreciation allocates asset cost over time. Loan payments are financing cash flows that can include principal and interest. They should not be substituted for each other in a budget.
questions: Which calculator should I use to set a selling price?
Use Markup if your target is a percentage above cost, or Margin if the target is a percentage of the selling price. Then check break-even sales using consistent cost assumptions.
Does a positive margin guarantee a profitable business?
No. The costs included in the calculation matter. A unit margin may leave out rent, payroll, financing, taxes and other overhead; include relevant expenses when reviewing the whole business.
Can I use these results for accounting or tax filings?
Use the outputs as planning illustrations. Accounting policies, tax rules, asset treatment and loan terms may require adjustments; confirm the treatment applicable to your business.
Does a high ROAS guarantee profit?

No. ROAS compares revenue with advertising expense. Product costs, fulfillment, transaction charges and other expenses affect what remains. Use the contribution-based modes with a consistent definition of costs, then review overhead and taxes separately.

heading: Everyday Calculators
title: Everyday Calculators - Percentages, Dates, Units & Discounts
description: Find lightweight calculators for percentages, scientific expressions, dates, unit conversion, tips, discounts and VAT. Choose a tool for everyday calculations.
intro: Choose a focused tool for everyday numbers: work out a percentage, compare dates, convert a unit or check a purchase total. Each calculator provides its own inputs and result explanation, so you can check the meaning of the answer as well as the number.
guides: Work with numbers and expressions

Use Percentage for percentage amounts and changes. Scientific Calculator handles supported mathematical expressions and functions; check angle units and expression syntax when using trigonometry or powers.
Compare dates or convert units
Use Date for the supported date intervals and date arithmetic. Unit Converter changes a value between compatible units; confirm the selected unit category and direction before using the result.
Check a bill or purchase

Use Tip & Bill Split for a tip and shared bill, Discount for a reduced price, and VAT for adding or removing an entered VAT rate. These tools use your inputs rather than looking up a merchant’s charges or current jurisdiction rules.
differences: Percentage change vs. percentage points
A rise from 10% to 15% is five percentage points, or a 50% increase relative to the original 10%. Choose the calculation that matches the question.
Discount vs. VAT
A discount reduces a price. VAT adds tax to a net amount or extracts included tax from a gross amount. Use consistent starting prices and check the order in which a seller applies adjustments.
Date intervals vs. unit conversion

Calendar intervals depend on the dates and the tool’s counting convention. Months are not all the same length, so a fixed number of days should not automatically be treated as an exact calendar month.
questions: Do I need an account to use these tools?
No account is needed. You can open a calculator directly, enter values and calculate. Optional Favorites are saved in the current browser rather than an online account.
Does VAT look up the correct tax rate for me?
No. Supply the applicable rate and select whether you are adding VAT or removing included VAT. Check the tax rules for the product and jurisdiction separately.
Why can a rounded result differ slightly from my own calculation?

Displayed precision may be shorter than the precision used internally. Check the selected units, percentage base and rounding before comparing results, especially when repeating a calculation across many items.
